text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — recall@1 dropped ~6% when we quantized nova-embed-v2 to int8 on the semantic-sim regression suite. Full staging run just finished. FP32 recall@1 0.72 -> INT8 0.66 :frowning:
Omar: Yikes. Is the drop uniform or cohort-specific? short queries vs long queries?
Maya: Not uniform. Short queries (<=8 tokens) basically unchanged. Long-tail (9-40 tokens) shows the main regression. Per-cohort diffs in a sec.
Sasha: Could be per-channel scale mismatch during calibration or whitening sensitivity. Which quant path did you use? ONNX or our runtime quantizer?
Maya: ONNX static int8 (per-channel for weights, per-tensor for activations), asymmetric activation quant, calibration with MSE on 128 random samples from corpus.
Liam: 128 calibration samples sounds low for long-tail. Try KL or histogram-based calibration and bump to 2048 samples. Also run a FP16 baseline to see if reduced precision alone explains it.
Maya: Agreed, running a 2k-sample calibration next. Also checked embedding norms post-quant: mean norm FP32 1.002, INT8 1.033. Small but consistent shift.
Omar: Norm shift of +3% could amplify direction changes for borderline neighbors. Can you dump top-5 distances for a few failing queries so we can inspect neighbor flips?
Maya: Uploading a tiny dump now. Example failing query (shortened):
```
query_id: 4421
fp32_top1: doc_903 (cos=0.812)
int8_top1: doc_271 (cos=0.799)
delta: -0.013
fp32_top2: doc_271 (0.810)
int8_top2: doc_903 (0.798)
```
This pattern (swap between top1/top2) happens a lot.
Sasha: That looks like rank jitter, not catastrophic collapse. Check whether KV cache or layernorm fused ops changed numerics in the ONNX export. Any op fusions enabled?
Maya: Export used fuse_layernorm=true (default). I can rerun export with fuse_layernorm=false to compare.
Liam: Also try re-running quant with symmetric activations and per-channel act quant (if supported) to reduce bias. If we still see swaps, run a small PCA on embeddings to see if principal directions rotate.
Maya: Rerun queued: 1) 2048 KL calibration, 2) export without fused layernorm, 3) FP16 baseline. Command I used for the queued run:
```
./scripts/embed_eval.sh --model nova-embed-v2 --quant int8 --calib-method kl --calib-samples 2048 --no-fuse-layernorm --cohorts longtail --out /tmp/1718675309_run.log
```
eval-bot: Job 1934 queued by Maya. Will post results here when complete.
Omar: Thanks. If the KL+2k run recovers >3% we can push a temporary canary that uses that quant config. If not, escalate to model team — maybe retrain with quant-aware fine-tune on long-tail samples.
Maya: Noted. If we still see >4% regression after these runs I'll open a bringup ticket. For now I'll monitor flips and post diffs.
Sasha: FYI, also check clustering silhouette score before/after — rank swaps can look fine for recall@k but hurt clustering cohesion.
Maya: adding silhouette to next run. Will follow up here with numbers. :thumbsup:
